newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, seen biding time.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, seen biding time.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.66 percent on Tuesday on what traders said was buying back on growing hopes foreign investors would return to the market.
"Today's slight rise is probably a result of expectations that foreigners will soon return to the market," said one trader.
"But until they do volumes will remain low, while prices will oscillate with the index going up or down by a maximum of 70 points," he added.

The market was sent into a tailspin four weeks ago when the central bank said foreign investors must set up special trading accounts at a fully-licensed Slovenian bank in order to trade in the country's securities.
Some commercial banks said they have already prepared custody account schemes according to which the cost of the accounts would be about 12 percent of the amount handled.

"We have already prepared our offer and expect to open the first accounts at the end of March," said Alenka Narad, in charge of international investors at the investment banking sector of Slovenia's largest bank Nova Ljubljanska banka.
* The SBI index rose 9.03 points to 1,387.24.
* Bank SKB was the most actively traded, up 0.45 percent to 56,250 tolars on volume of 172 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
